**Shift Quality:** 7/10. Coverage excellent, compliance near-complete except for unconfirmed POC notification. Recommend ops follow-up on POC status post-shift.

Shift 06/24-06/25: Rosa maintained solid presence throughout 8-hour overnight. Arrived on-site, checked in with POC (Naomi) regarding pre-existing fence breach on Chalfonte side. Shift 6/23 10PM–6AM complete. Guard Rosa Nguyen (7326) delivered clean 8-hour shift. Recommended for future assignments.

site_notes.content: Guard confirmed the post binder is still not present on post and noted it is where daily paperwork is recorded. This is the second consecutive shift without the binder, leaving the guard without the standard on-site documentation log.

Guard did not have site POC contact numbers available on post at shift open and was unable to reach anyone by phone due to poor cell signal. The communication gap with designated site contacts continues.
Guard reported upon arrival that they have not received a post binder. Written site-specific protocols and instructions are unavailable to the guard at the post.
Post binder not present at post

Guard checked in with on-site team member Tinika upon arrival rather than the designated site contacts (Naomi, Nate, Jacob), whom the guard was unfamiliar with. In-person access was managed through Tinika; the gap with the designated POC list continues unresolved.

Guard attempted to reach the designated site contacts upon arrival and was unable to reach any of them — only dispatch and the outgoing guard were reached. The communication gap with site POCs continues.
The construction contractor was confirmed departed from the site at 22:16. Saturday July 11 falls within the tracked Saturday work schedule running through July 25.

On-site supervisor Shaun confirmed a construction team will be working on-site for the next three Saturdays (July 11, 18, and 25). Shaun is remaining on-site to oversee the crew throughout each of these shifts rather than departing at shift open.
Construction crew on-site Saturdays through July 25 — Shaun supervising

Guard successfully checked in with on-site supervisor Shaun at shift open. Shaun is overseeing the construction crew and was present on-site — he is not one of the three previously listed contacts (Naomi, Nate, Jacob). His presence provided a functioning in-person point of contact for this shift, though the status of the listed contact numbers remains unresolved.
Guard attempted to reach site contacts Nate and Naomi and reported being unable to get hold of either. The communication gap with designated site POCs continues.
Guard confirmed upon arrival that all fence sections are back in place and the perimeter is intact with no issues noted. All sections that had been down are now restored.

Guard attempted to reach all three designated site contacts (Naomi, Nate, Jacob) at shift open — none answered. A follow-up contact attempt mid-shift also yielded no response. The communication gap with site POCs continues unresolved.
Guard confirmed the John Deere loader lights are off. Both reports this shift directly verify the lights are no longer on, closing out the condition that had persisted for approximately 14 days.
Guard attempted to reach site contacts at shift open and received no answer from either. The communication gap with designated POCs continues.
Guard attempted to reach all three designated site contacts — Naomi, Nate, and Jacob — upon shift open. None were reachable. This marks another shift with no available POC contact.
Guard reached out to Jacob at shift open and awaited his response. Naomi and Nate were not mentioned as successfully contacted. The communication gap with site POCs continues.

No site POC was present on-site at shift start. Keys and radio were retrieved from the vehicle without a client representative handoff. None of the designated contacts (Naomi, Nate, Jacob) were on-site to complete the arrival protocol.
Guard attempted to reach site contact Nate upon shift open and again mid-shift; no response was received throughout the shift.
Guard confirmed the gates are back up and all is secure. The officer positioned on the west side independently verified the same — perimeter is restored.

Guard reported not having a site POC contact number available on post. In-person contact with Naomi was made upon arrival and the shift proceeded normally, but no telephone contact number for site management was accessible to the guard.
Guard attempted to reach site contact Naomi upon arrival and reported no response.
A Northgate-branded vehicle (plate KTP-4417) was again found on-site without authorization at the start of the shift. The guard documented the vehicle with seven photographs.
Guard's opening walkthrough confirmed the west side gate breach remains present. The site was otherwise reported clear.

Guard confirmed the downed fence area was still a focal concern and maintained primary posted coverage there throughout the overnight shift, conducting exterior rounds with that area as the priority station.

Guard found approximately 14 perimeter fence sections down on arrival. Worked to restore the fence, putting approximately 20 sections back up; perimeter reported mostly restored and the site otherwise clear, with no signs of active intrusion.

A full section of the west side building gate was found completely down, blown over by high winds. Equipment is visible from outside the perimeter, creating an active access vulnerability. Supervisors were notified and the guard implemented heightened patrols of the affected area for the remainder of the shift. The guard noted that given the July 4th holiday weekend, on-site repair is unlikely in the near term; all weekend shifts have been briefed to continue patrolling the west gate area until the breach is addressed.
West side building gate section down — perimeter breach

Guard reported that a section of the tennis court gate had fallen and brought the condition to supervisory attention at shift end. Physical state of the gate section was not further described; on-site inspection is warranted.
Tennis court gate section fallen
Guard attempted to reach all three designated site contacts upon arrival. Naomi and Nate remained unreachable; Jacob was successfully reached by phone and the shift handoff was completed.

Upon arrival, a Northgate-branded Chevy Trax (plate KTP-4417) was again found parked on-site without authorization. The guard documented the vehicle with multiple photographs, including clear plate visibility.
Guard requested site contact numbers and reported being unable to reach anyone due to poor cell service on site. The communication gap with site contacts continues.

Guard attempted to reach all three designated site contacts — Naomi, Nate, and Jacob — using the numbers listed in the job instructions. None of the numbers connected. Emergency contact coverage for this site is currently unavailable through the numbers on file and should be updated.
Site POC contact numbers non-functional

Guard confirmed the John Deere loader lights were still on during the opening walkthrough. Equipment was observed with no signs of tampering; the condition persists and its cause remains unidentified.
Guard reported the walkie-talkie is still not working properly this shift. Primary communication via phone remained operational and the post stayed connected throughout.

Exterior lights on the John Deere loader were on upon guard arrival at 9:45 PM and remained on throughout the overnight shift. The guard observed the equipment continuously and confirmed no tampering. The lights draw nighttime attention to the equipment and their cause has not been identified.
John Deere loader lights left on — equipment under observation
Guard confirmed this shift that the fence on the Chalfonte side has been repaired.

Guard identified a breach in the perimeter fence on the Chalfonte side upon arrival. The breach was assessed as small. Photos were taken, POC Naomi was notified, and the guard positioned at the location to maintain close watch for the entirety of the shift. No unauthorized access through the breach was observed.
Fence breach on Chalfonte side
Guard reported a flat tire on the front right passenger side of the Jeep located in the inner court of the site. Condition was reported at shift end.
Flat tire on Jeep in inner court equipment zone
A flat tire was discovered on Buick patrol vehicle 45 at the site (15055 Hubble) during the overnight shift. The condition was reported for ops follow-up; vehicle mobility status was not confirmed.
Flat tire on patrol vehicle 45 at site
At 23:28, the guard observed and chased away juveniles attempting to climb over the main entrance gate. The group dispersed without gaining entry; no breach occurred.

Guard's walkie-talkie battery died during on-site patrol at 20:23. No backup battery or charger available on post. Guard switched to cell phone contact for remainder of shift. Equipment failure left post without standard radio communication for approximately 5 hours until shift end.
Walkie-talkie communication failure; no charger or backup on post

During the midday patrol, an unauthorized vehicle was found on the property — a white Chevrolet Trax, Michigan plate EAD 0682, with 'Northgate' company branding visible on the plate. The vehicle was present on-site and documented with sixteen photographs covering vehicle details and interior.

Guard confirmed the site gate operates as a 'dummy lock' — it is configured to appear secured but is not truly locked. The design is intentional to allow emergency vehicle access. The gate nonetheless remains unsecured at the site level, consistent with prior shift observations.

A single occupant in a blue van (plate EYX 9003) drove to the back of the site at approximately 9:30 AM and removed bricks from the demolition debris pile. The guard witnessed the theft, documented the plate, and submitted a photo. This represents an escalation from prior approach attempts to a completed unauthorized removal of materials.
Guard confirmed the east side perimeter fence is back up at the start of the shift and submitted photo documentation. Fence repair is verified.

A woman approached the site and requested bricks from the building. She was denied access and informed of the no-trespass policy and the site's history of theft. She understood and departed immediately. This is consistent with the pattern of unauthorized interest in the property and its materials.
Individuals approaching site attempting to remove building materials

A school building door was found propped open with a 2x4 during the overnight shift. The guard removed the wedge and closed the door. The deliberate propping — rather than a door left ajar — suggests an established on-site crew practice. On an active Vantage Storage site, this creates a security gap and warrants attention from site management to ensure crews are not leaving building access points unsecured.
School building door propped open by site workers
